jobs.title: AVP, Actuarial AI & Data Governance
jobs.description:
As AVP, Actuarial AI & Data Governance
, you will lead the strategy, governance and enablement required to accelerate responsible adoption of AI and strengthen data capabilities across Actuarial.

Reporting to the VP, Actuarial Innovation, you will partner with Actuarial leaders, enterprise AI and Data teams, Data Governance, Technology, Risk and other partners to establish and embed data governance, along with lead the shift from individual AI use cases to embedding AI and trusted data into core actuarial workflows and ways of working.

You will lead the evolution of Actuarial data governance, establishing clear ownership and stewardship, strengthening data quality management, and creating greater transparency and accountability for the data that underpins critical actuarial processes. You will work across Actuarial and enterprise partners to ensure data issues are identified, prioritized and addressed, while aligning Actuarial practices with broader enterprise data standards and governance.

You will also establish the frameworks and capabilities that enable Actuarial to innovate responsibly and at scale, including AI portfolio prioritization, citizen-led development, responsible AI governance, capability building and value realization. You will provide a trusted view of the Actuarial AI portfolio and help leaders determine where to invest, accelerate, scale, redirect or stop initiatives based on business value, feasibility and risk.

The role will be instrumental in developing an AI- and data-enabled actuarial function, improving productivity, quality and speed of insight while strengthening the governance and accountability required to maintain trust in actuarial data and AI-enabled processes.

Position Responsibilities

AI & Data Strategy and Transformation

Develop and execute the Actuarial AI and Data strategy, aligned with broader Actuarial priorities and enterprise AI, Data and Technology strategies.
Partner with Actuarial leaders to identify and redesign priority workflows where AI, automation and better use of data can materially improve how actuarial work is performed.
Establish a clear roadmap for AI and Data capability development, balancing near-term opportunities with longer-term transformation priorities.

AI Portfolio Governance & Value Realization

Establish and evolve a transparent governance and prioritization framework for the Actuarial AI portfolio, including intake, assessment, prioritization, decision rights and pathways for delivery.
Maintain a trusted view of the AI portfolio, including strategic alignment, expected value, delivery progress, dependencies, risks and realized outcomes.
Lead structured portfolio reviews and provide recommendations on which opportunities should be accelerated, scaled, redirected, paused or stopped.
Develop and maintain a value-realization framework with measurable baselines and outcomes,

AI Enablement, Adoption & Capability Building

Build Actuarial AI literacy and capability through a structured learning, experimentation and adoption program.
Partner with learning and talent teams to embed AI capabilities into broader Actuarial skill development.
Drive the transition from individual AI use cases toward repeatable capabilities and transformed workflows that can be adopted and scaled across the function.

Data Governance & Data Capability

Define and evolve the data governance framework for Actuarial, aligned with enterprise policies, standards and controls.
Establish clear data ownership and stewardship models for critical actuarial data, with explicit accountability for data quality and effective use.
Develop practical mechanisms for identifying, logging, prioritizing and resolving material data-quality issues.
Partner with enterprise Data, Technology and business teams to improve the accessibility, reliability and usability of data required by Actuarial.
Provide governance and strategic direction without duplicating enterprise ownership of data platforms and technical infrastructure.

Leadership & Stakeholder Engagement

Serve as a strategic advisor to senior Actuarial leaders on AI, data and emerging technology, translating complex topics into clear choices, implications and actions.
Engage leaders to establish shared ownership of workflow transformation and measurable business outcomes
Lead and develop a small, high-impact team and extend its reach through partnerships across Actuarial, enterprise AI, Data, Technology, HR/Learning and other functions.
Communicate progress, outcomes, risks and strategic choices clearly to senior leadership.

What We Are Looking For

FSA/FCIA designation, or equivalent
Deep understanding of actuarial processes, supported by hands-on experience across core actuarial workflows.
Strong understanding of how AI, advanced analytics and modern data capabilities can be applied to knowledge-intensive business processes.
Leadership and management skills, leading both direct and indirect teams
Strong business acumen with an aptitude for strategic, critical, and analytical thinking
Strong verbal and written communications skills
Strong relationship management skills and ability to work within and across departments
Understanding the needs of various stakeholders across the organization
Ability to manage multiple projects of varying priorities levels and scope

When You Join Our Team

We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want.
We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words.
As part of our global team, we’ll support you in shaping the future you want to see.

Job Description Summary

The Director of Customer Services and Informatics is a senior leadership position within UBC Facilities. The Director provides strategic leadership for Facilities customer service function, customer service plan, business project management, business analysis, informatics, enterprise maintenance management system (EMMS), facilities information and inventory systems, change management, call centre management and clerical support services. This role develops strategic objectives, implements and monitors procedures and policies that enable Facilities to meet or exceed agreed customer service standards across the entire campus. In addition, this division provides all business units within Facilities the necessary business support both by providing the necessary analytics and analysis to ensure continuous improvements continue across the department. The Director is responsible for the development and sustainment of the Facilities Emergency Management Plan.

The Director of Customer Services and Informatics is the Facilities representative for customer engagement, business projects and initiatives, space inventory data, building and infrastructure records drawings and information, analytics, reporting, technology and continuous improvement initiatives. They partner with Information Technology (IT) and Safety and Risk Services (SRS) - Emergency Management, Project Management Office (PMO), Integrated Service Centre (ISC), Communications & Engagement for strategic alignment and resource allocation.

The Director leads a workforce of approximately 35 staff in professional and unionized positions. Prepares strategic and business plans and supports an annual Facilities budget of approximately $150M.

Organizational Status

This position reports directly to the Associate Vice-President, Facilities, and serves as a member of the Facilities Leadership team. Works closely with other Directors, Senior Managers, and Managers as well as other department‘s leadership teams. This position is the senior leader within Facilities responsible for implementing business transformational initiatives with the support of other divisions, monitoring operational progress through the analysis and reporting of information to guide evidence-based decision-making.

Leads the facilities information and inventory systems function, including university space inventory data, building and infrastructure record drawings, key plans, emergency response plans, and maintenance manuals.
Provides direction and implements change management methodologies to effectively lead and optimize key projects across Facilities.
Mentors and coaches change management in relation to the implementation of business initiatives.
Liaises with academic, administrative and ancillary customers, engineers, architects and external clients to ensure that the facilities needs of the university are being met.
Supports and provides direction to the Senior Facilities Manager in providing strategic leadership to the Facilities Managers working in the geographic zone model. Through the Senior Facilities Manager, oversees the delivery of equal, consistent and effectively prioritized service delivery within the campus zones.
Provides strategic leadership on sustainment of Facilities and University information systems in support of enterprise maintenance management, asset management, stores inventory, space inventory, records drawings, records management, and project management.
Provides strategic leadership and/or oversees development of innovative business solutions and services that integrate data and reporting capabilities to augment decision-making.
Oversees work of various teams performing quality testing of data and information and reconciling across sources, presenting facts and evidence in dashboards to assist in effective evidence-based decision making.
Provides strategic leadership to the Facilities Service Centre who are responsible for handling inbound and outbound calls regarding buildings and grounds.
Responsible for administrative/clerical support services for the Facilities group.
Provides direction in the completion of regulatory and skills development training for all staff within Facilities which includes developing plans, implementing and evaluating, department-wide strategies.
Leads and directs the development of the Facilities Emergency Management Plan, including emergency preparedness exercises for the department in collaboration with SRS, Emergency Management.
Works with SRS and implements consistent health, safety and environmental initiatives, which, includes safety committee, accident investigations, safety training and safety recommendations within the Customer Services and Informatics division.
Responsible for human resource practices including recruitment, orientation, training, performance evaluation, discipline, labor relations and dismissal within the Customer Services and Informatics division in collaboration with Human Resources.
Performs other related duties, including but not limited to:
Representing Facilities on various university committees. Develops working relationships and partnerships with key stakeholders across UBC.
Acting on behalf of the Associate Vice-President, Facilities.

Consequence of Error/Judgement

Facilities plays a key role in enabling the University to achieve its goal of becoming one of the world‘s leading universities. The Director Customer Services and Informatics position is critical to the success of Facilities and the complex services that it provides. The Director must apply judgment, tact and discretion due to the broad and extensive implications for success in the areas of facilities management, project management, business analysis, informatics, information system management, change management, call centre management and clerical support services. The Director plays an important part in the formulation, alignment and implementation of the strategic initiatives and managing the outcomes and impacts on operations and the services they provide.

WHO WE ARE

GreenShield is a proudly Canadian, national non-profit health care and insurance organization, driven by our mission of Better Health for All. As a non-profit social enterprise without shareholders, we reinvest our excess earnings to directly support underserved communities. Through GreenShield Cares, we positively impacted the health and well-being of over one million Canadians between 2020 and 2025. What’s driving us now is the commitment to measurably impact an additional three million Canadians by 2030 – across mental health, essential medicines, and chronic disease management – through scalable initiatives that deliver meaningful change in pursuit of our mission of Better Health for All.
At GreenShield, our culture is where purpose meets passion and performance. Our teams work as one to deliver meaningful, measurable impact for the people and communities we serve.

About The Lacroix Medical Group

A leader in private medicine in Quebec, the Lacroix Medical Group comprises three rapidly growing divisions:

Medical Clinics
Operating Rooms
Biomedical Laboratory

The organization has experienced strong and sustained growth since its founding in 2009 and currently employs nearly 350 people. As part of its strategic plan, the Group aims to accelerate its national and international development.

OUR MISSION

To be the benchmark in private healthcare.

OUR VALUES

Passion | Respect | Integrity | Commitment | Innovation.

The Mandate

In a context of sustained growth and transformation of its activities, Lacroix Medical Group is seeking a Director of Information Technology who will actively contribute to the organization's technological evolution.

Reporting directly to the President and CEO, the Director of IT plays a strategic role across the entire network. They are responsible for defining, structuring, and developing the IT function to effectively support the organization's operations, growth, and ambitions.

They provide leadership for technology strategy, infrastructure, business systems, cybersecurity, data governance, digital transformation, and artificial intelligence.

He is also responsible for the performance of his team and the organization's technology partner ecosystem. This role is for an experienced, business-oriented, and results-driven IT leader who can combine strategic vision with excellent execution. Your Key Responsibilities IT Strategy and Governance: Define and deploy the IT vision and master plan in line with the strategic, operational, and financial priorities of Groupe médical Lacroix. Advise senior management on investments, risks, and key technological choices.

Performance and Business Continuity

Ensure the performance, robustness, and high availability of the infrastructure and technology platforms essential to the network's medical and administrative activities, including ERP, CRM, DME, LIS, SaaS, and cloud environments.

Digital Transformation, Data, and Artificial Intelligence

Identify and prioritize initiatives to transform the organization through technology, data valorization, automation, and artificial intelligence. Lead major technology projects and ensure their effective integration into operations.

Cybersecurity and Risk Management

Maintain high standards in cybersecurity, information protection, redundancy, and business continuity in an environment where system availability and the protection of medical data are critical.

Leadership and Organizational Performance

Lead and develop a competent, autonomous, and accountable IT team. Establish clear objectives and performance indicators, ensure rigorous budget management, and optimize the contribution of suppliers, consultants, and technology partners.

An Executive Role Close to Operations

At Lacroix Medical Group, technology must meet the realities on the ground.

The IT Director will therefore need to maintain close contact with the various business units and network teams to understand their needs, anticipate challenges, and ensure that technological solutions contribute concretely to operational performance and service quality.

The position consequently requires excellent mobility. The successful candidate will be required to travel regularly throughout the Lacroix network in Quebec to meet with teams, support projects, and remain connected to the operational realities of the various facilities.

This on-the-ground presence is an essential component of the role and not an occasional responsibility.

The mandate expressly includes regular visits to service points.

The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for an experienced manager with a strong business acumen and excellent technological expertise, recognized for their leadership, judgment, and ability to drive organizational growth.

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

A bachelor's degree in computer engineering, computer science, or a related field;
15 to 20 years of experience in information technology, including a minimum of 5 years in a management role;
Mastery of software architecture and project management;
A solid understanding of multi-site and cloud infrastructures;
Good knowledge of SaaS environments and major business platforms: ERP, CRM, financial systems, telephony, Microsoft 365, and others;
A thorough understanding of the issues cybersecurity, data governance and valorization, and artificial intelligence;
Proven experience in team management and development;
Recognized leadership in transformation and change management;
Ability to prioritize, make decisions, and manage effectively in a complex and evolving environment;
Excellent business acumen and the ability to communicate technological issues to senior management;
Fluency in French and English, both written and spoken;
A valid driver's license, a vehicle, and significant availability for regular travel throughout the network.

The Leader Profile We Are Looking For

Beyond technological expertise, we are looking for someone who stands out for their ability to mobilize, structure, and deliver.

A positive and committed leader with a strong sense of Accountability, the ability to build high-performing teams, manage rigorously, challenge the status quo, and transform technological challenges into concrete solutions for the business. The IT Director must be equally comfortable discussing strategy with senior management and understanding the challenges faced by teams in the field. SIRIUS INSTRUMENTATION AND CONTROLS INC.

THE ORGANIZATION

Sirius designs and manufactures chemical injection systems and instrumentation packages for upstream and midstream oil and gas operators. Their equipment runs in some of the harshest production environments in the world - Western Canada, the Permian, and increasingly the Middle East, Africa and Latin America - where precision matters and downtime costs money. Their technologies help eliminate greenhouse gas emissions, improve injection accuracy, and reduce manpower and chemical costs - two of their customers’ largest expenses. The portfolio includes solar-powered and AC chemical injection systems, environmentally friendly tank systems, and advanced automation technologies.

Founded in April 2003 in Alberta, Canada, Sirius is headquartered in Edmonton with U.S. operations in Midland, Texas (operating as Sirius Controls Inc.) since 2017. Sirius is a registered corporation with APEGA (Association of Professional Engineers) and was awarded the 2018 “Clean Technology Innovation” Award by CETAC-West. Since December 2024, Sirius has been backed by a private equity sponsor and is executing a multi-year growth plan that targets a doubling of revenue across both countries, while adding key international markets.

Sirius’s Core Values define their culture, drive their work, and guide their commitment to excellence. They are the operating standard for every member of the team - and the Vice President, Finance is expected to model and reinforce them.

Core Values:

Continuous Innovation
: Innovation begins with listening to understand and transforms curiosity into impactful solutions. It is a continuous improvement loop that channels learning back into our products, processes, and people.
Integrity:
We do what we say we will do. We take responsibility for our actions and own our commitments to become trusted advisors that clients rely on.
Collaboration:
We achieve excellence by working together with trust, humility, open communication, and a shared purpose. Collaboration means ownership across every step of the process.

For more information on Sirius Instrumentation & Controls, please visit their website at: https://www.siriuscontrols.com/.

THE OPPORTUNITY

The Vice President, Finance (“VP Finance”) is a senior finance leader accountable for the integrity, accuracy, and effectiveness of accounting, reporting, and financial operations across both Sirius entities: Sirius Instrumentation and Controls Inc. (Canadian parent) and Sirius Controls Inc. (U.S. subsidiary). The VP Finance also partners closely with leaders across the Company to strengthen effectiveness and optimize performance.

Reporting directly to the Chief Financial Officer (“CFO”), the VP Finance serves as the CFO’s deputy and designated backup, ensuring continuity across board, sponsor, lender, banking, insurance, and audit relationships, and acting on the CFO’s behalf as delegated or required.

The VP Finance retains direct ownership of the accounting function while progressively delegating close and transactional execution to the Assistant Controller as that role continues to develop. The scope will expand across financial planning and analysis, treasury, tax compliance coordination, and strategic finance, including key initiatives such as ERP implementation.

RESPONSIBILITIES

In support of the organization's strategic objectives, the successful candidate will be accountable for the following key responsibilities:

Financial Reporting and Technical Accounting

Accountable for the consolidated month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close across both entities, including intercompany eliminations and FX translation (IAS 21); ensure timely, accurate consolidated reporting under IFRS.
Accountable for all IFRS technical positions including but not limited to - IFRS 15 revenue recognition, IAS 2 standard costing and WIP valuation, IFRS 16 leases, IAS 12 deferred tax, and IFRS 3 acquisition accounting carry-forward; prepare technical memos and defend positions to auditors.
Responsible for the primary external audit relationship - planning, PBC management, technical defense, and year-end coordination.
Ensure compliance with tax, regulatory, and Board of Directors-specific reporting requirements.

Internal Controls, Risk, and Governance

Responsible for the internal control environment across all transactional cycles (revenue/receivables, purchases/payables, payroll, inventory, fixed assets, treasury, close and reporting); and progress the framework toward SOX-lite (COSO 2013).
Establish and maintain accounting policies, procedures, and controls documentation.
Partner with the CFO on risk management and audit committee reporting.

Accounting Operations and Delegation

Accountable for the accuracy and completeness of accounts receivable, accounts payable, payroll, inventory, and treasury activities across both entities.
Progressively transition close execution, transactional review and AR/AP Admins to the Assistant Controller against a defined development plan, retaining review authority and overall accountability for the function.
Supervise tax compliance - GST/HST, U.S. state sales and use tax, and cross-border requirements-coordinating with external advisors on transfer pricing, withholding, and treaty application.
Collaborating with sales department, legal counsel and clients to ensure timely and optimal Master Services Agreements.

Financial Planning and Analysis; Board and Sponsor Reporting

Responsible for the completion of the board reporting packages: monthly flash, quarterly board pack, sponsor reporting, and covenant compliance certificates.
Build and lead the FP&A capability - annual budget, rolling 12-month forecast (quarterly), budget-versus-actual and variance analysis, and KPI reporting - to support decision-making.
Assume Budget Master role while partnering with the CFO to deliver the annual budget.
Provide insight on financial performance, margins, working capital, and risk areas as a Partner to the executive team.

Treasury and Cash Management

Responsible for working capital management, and CAD/USD exposure monitoring.
Manage day-to-day banking relationships, credit facility reporting, and intercompany funding, escalating covenant and liquidity matters to the CFO.

Systems and Process Improvement

Lead the finance workstreams of the ERP implementation - requirements, chart of accounts design, data migration, UAT, cutover, and post-go-live stabilization - through the transition from QuickBooks.
Collaborate with supporting the Plant Controller and Senior Vice President Operations, operationalize standard costing in the make-to-order manufacturing environment, including BOM accuracy, overhead absorption, and variance analysis.
Drive process automation and continuous improvement of the close, reporting cadence, and documentation base to support margin improvement.

Leadership and Team Development

Manage, mentor, and scale the accounting team; foster a culture of accountability, process improvement, and cross-functional collaboration.
Develop the Assistant Controller on a defined succession track toward financial controller-level ownership of the close; establish SOPs, training milestones, and cross-training pairs.
Build a documented and defensible finance function.

Strategic Partnership and CFO Redundancy

Act as the CFO’s deputy: represent Finance with the board, sponsor, lenders, and auditors as delegated, and assume the CFO’s operating responsibilities in the CFO’s absence.
Support M&A activity - diligence, integration, and acquisition accounting - including vendor due diligence and quality of earnings readiness.
Support international expansion structuring (Middle East and beyond) with external advisors as it progresses.
Collaborate with the sales, operations, and engineering teams, to be a Business Partner supporting financial decision making, cost savings initiatives, and strategic decision making

MEASURES OF SUCCESS

Audit-Ready Financial Reporting:
Consolidated IFRS reporting is delivered accurately and on schedule, with a clean external audit and no material adjustments or control deficiencies.
Scalable, Audit-Ready Finance Function:
Strong controls, clear documentation, and a successfully implemented ERP that position the business well.
Seamless CFO Continuity and Team Succession:
The VP Finance is trusted by the Board, sponsor, lenders, and auditors as the CFO’s deputy, while the Assistant Controller progresses to independent ownership of the close.

THE INDIVIDUAL

Given the pivotal role this individual will be expected to play in achieving the strategic objectives of the company and in supporting the success of the organization, it is essential that the successful candidate possess the following education, experience, competencies and attributes:

Education

A university degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, or a related field is required; an MBA is considered an asset.
Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation in good standing is required.
Strong working knowledge of IFRS is required, including the application of complex technical accounting standards.
Knowledge of U.S. GAAP or cross-border reporting experience would be considered an asset.
Commitment to ongoing professional development, particularly in IFRS, tax, and financial systems.

Experience

Must-have:

A minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in accounting and finance, including senior leadership responsibility for the accounting and reporting function.
Demonstrated expertise in IFRS, including consolidated reporting across multiple entities, intercompany eliminations, foreign currency translation, and preparation of technical accounting positions.
Proven experience leading the external audit relationship and delivering clean, timely audits.
Track record of building and strengthening internal controls, accounting policies, and finance processes.
Experience preparing Board, lender, or investor reporting, including budgeting, forecasting, and variance analysis.
Demonstrated success leading, mentoring, and developing accounting teams, including succession planning and delegation.

Nice-to-have:

Manufacturing experience is strongly preferred, ideally within a make-to-order or engineered products environment, with a solid understanding of standard costing, inventory valuation, and overhead absorption.
Experience in a private equity-backed or sponsor-owned organization, vendor due diligence, or quality of earnings processes.
Experience leading or supporting an ERP implementation, particularly a transition from an entry-level system such as QuickBooks.
Exposure to U.S. GAAP and cross-border Canada/U.S. operations, including sales and use tax, transfer pricing, and withholding considerations.
Experience managing banking and credit facility relationships, including covenant compliance.
Involvement in M&A activity, acquisition accounting, or international expansion.

Competencies and Knowledge

Technical Accounting Expertise
: Deep, current knowledge of IFRS with the confidence to research, document, and defend complex technical positions with auditors.
Financial Leadership and Insight
: Ability to translate financial results into clear, actionable insight on performance, margins, working capital, and risk.
Controls and Governance
: Strong understanding of internal control frameworks (including COSO) and the discipline to build a finance function that is well documented and audit-ready.
Systems and Process Optimization
: Experience modernizing finance processes and systems, with a practical approach to automation, ERP implementation, and continuous improvement.
Business Partnership:
Skilled at collaborating with Operations, Sales, and Engineering to support sound decision-making and drive cost and margin improvements.
Communication and Influence
: Able to communicate complex financial matters clearly and credibly to the Board, sponsor, lenders, and non-financial leader

Delta Group is a Western Canadian wholesale distribution and solutions platform serving waterworks and water infrastructure, agricultural irrigation, pumps and motors, water treatment, wastewater and related markets. Through acquisitions and organic growth, the group has an opportunity to integrate supply-chain practices while maintaining the market knowledge and relationships of its operating businesses.

Position mandate

Lead Delta’s end-to-end group supply-chain strategy, with executive accountability for procurement, inventory investment and quality, demand planning, vendor economics, replenishment and network efficiency. Build one disciplined operating framework across multiple companies and branches without impairing customer service or project execution. This is an operational change-leadership position, not simply a senior purchasing appointment. This role can be based in Calgary or Chilliwack, BC.

Group supply-chain strategy and governance

Design and implement group-wide policies for inventory, purchasing, approvals, stock allocation and supplier engagement.
Clarify central versus local authority, escalation rules, exception management and performance accountability.
Partner closely with General Managers, Finance, sales and operations; lead monthly supply-chain performance reviews.
Integrate acquired businesses and branch practices into a scalable operating model.

Inventory investment, productivity and controls

Own group inventory productivity, target-setting and action plans by branch, segment, category and SKU.
Drive reduction of excess, obsolete, slow-moving and duplicate inventory through transfers, vendor returns, disposition and prevention.
Set service-sensitive reorder points, safety stocks, inventory classifications and replenishment policies.
Establish consistent cycle counts, inventory accuracy and inventory ownership controls; coordinate valuation and reserves with Finance.
Protect strategic, seasonal and critical long-lead stock while improving inventory turns and cash generation.

Procurement and supplier management

Coordinate category strategy, purchasing scale, approval limits and controls for committed purchases.
Negotiate supplier terms, pricing, rebates, freight, returns, vendor-managed/consignment arrangements and service commitments.
Implement supplier scorecards and contingency planning for critical products and manufacturers.
Improve purchase-order visibility, interbranch-first decisions and special-order controls; prevent unsupported speculative buys.
Maintain the relationships needed to protect exclusive lines and the commercial advantage of Delta’s technical product portfolios.

Demand planning and major projects

Create rolling forecasting processes using sales patterns, seasonality, known projects and credible customer commitments.
Differentiate recurring wholesale replenishment from project-specific purchasing for pivots, pipe, pumps and engineered packages.
Coordinate purchasing with project managers, installation schedules, deposits and supplier lead times.

Establish item-master governance: duplicates, naming, UOMs, vendor references, product attributes, inactive SKUs and status.
Build reliable dashboards for aging, turns, fill rate, demand accuracy, outstanding POs, project stock and supplier performance.
Drive practical system-based replenishment and useful automation rather than spreadsheets without accountability.

Working capital and financial accountability

Develop annual and rolling plans for inventory cash release, purchasing efficiencies and inventory-related operating costs.
Coordinate with VP Finance on cash forecasting, open commitments, vendor terms and independently verified savings.
Evaluate investments against inventory carrying cost, service levels, gross margin, liquidity and project risks.
Report monthly to the CEO with financial outcomes, constraints and corrective actions.

People leadership and transformation

Hire, coach and hold accountable functional leaders and analysts as approved.
Work constructively with GMs while challenging unsupported inventory and purchasing decisions.
Lead branch-level adoption through training, site visits, clear metrics and consistent follow-through.

Strong track record in vendor negotiations, category strategy, purchase controls and operational change after acquisitions.
Commercial understanding of distribution gross margin, inventory carrying cost, cash conversion, stockouts and service economics.
Hands-on experience implementing effective ERP-based replenishment and master-data management.
Ability to lead effectively through influence and formal authority in decentralized technical distribution businesses.
Relevant degree or equivalent operating experience; SCMP, CSCP or CPIM an asset; regular Western Canadian travel required.

Preferred background

Industrial, waterworks, plumbing, pump and motor, agricultural equipment, irrigation, electrical or HVAC wholesale distribution; acquisition integration; regional distribution network optimization; and balancing project procurement with standard branch replenishment.
Leadership profile
Commercially astute, financially disciplined and decisive; credible at branch and warehouse level; analytically strong, capable of difficult conversations with respected GMs, and equally focused on supplier relationships, customer service and sustainable cash release. Comfortable with ambiguous data but unwilling to accept unsupported conclusions.

Key measures of success

Inventory investment and turns by business, branch and category, adjusted for commercial conditions and service needs.
Aged, obsolete and duplicate stock reduction; inventory accuracy and shrinkage.
Working-capital release and annualized procurement/freight/rebate savings validated by Finance.
Customer fill rates, on-time delivery, backorders and project material availability.
Purchasing compliance, forecasting reliability, supplier performance and inventory transfer effectiveness.
Business Central item-master quality, supply-chain reporting and adoption of replenishment processes.
Strength and accountability of supply-chain leadership and branch operating practices.

By 90 days: institute buying authority, interbranch-first controls, aged-inventory program and CEO dashboard. Months 4–6: demonstrate measurable cash release, supplier and forecasting improvements. By 12 months: deliver sustained financial and service outcomes and an approved second-year improvement plan. Specific financial targets will be agreed with the CEO and VP Finance after verifying opening conditions.

The opportunity is to shape the supply-chain economics of a substantial Western Canadian technical distribution platform, turn scale into meaningful procurement and inventory advantage, and build a disciplined, scalable organization. The role carries senior leadership visibility, operating influence and direct accountability for measurable results.

Job Description Summary

The Director of Customer Services and Informatics is a senior leadership position within UBC Facilities. The Director provides strategic leadership for Facilities customer service function, customer service plan, business project management, business analysis, informatics, enterprise maintenance management system (EMMS), facilities information and inventory systems, change management, call centre management and clerical support services. This role develops strategic objectives, implements and monitors procedures and policies that enable Facilities to meet or exceed agreed customer service standards across the entire campus. In addition, this division provides all business units within Facilities the necessary business support both by providing the necessary analytics and analysis to ensure continuous improvements continue across the department. The Director is responsible for the development and sustainment of the Facilities Emergency Management Plan.

The Director of Customer Services and Informatics is the Facilities representative for customer engagement, business projects and initiatives, space inventory data, building and infrastructure records drawings and information, analytics, reporting, technology and continuous improvement initiatives. They partner with Information Technology (IT) and Safety and Risk Services (SRS) - Emergency Management, Project Management Office (PMO), Integrated Service Centre (ISC), Communications & Engagement for strategic alignment and resource allocation.

The Director leads a workforce of approximately 35 staff in professional and unionized positions. Prepares strategic and business plans and supports an annual Facilities budget of approximately $150M.

Organizational Status

This position reports directly to the Associate Vice-President, Facilities, and serves as a member of the Facilities Leadership team. Works closely with other Directors, Senior Managers, and Managers as well as other department‘s leadership teams. This position is the senior leader within Facilities responsible for implementing business transformational initiatives with the support of other divisions, monitoring operational progress through the analysis and reporting of information to guide evidence-based decision-making.

Work Performed

Provides strategic leadership to the Facilities Leadership team through the Customer Services and Informatics division to execute a full range of department-wide services to meet targets and objectives of the Strategic Plan. This includes supporting and developing business plans; ensuring consistent and effective implementation; enhancing integration; standardizing services and business practices; maximizing efficiencies and cost savings.
Responsible for business transformational projects through assessment, analysis, design and implementation; champions the implementation of change management initiatives, process and execution.
Leads the development of a Monitoring Framework with key performance indicators for each unit within the department and develops remedial and continuous improvement plans in relation to results. This framework includes leading and lagging indicators and an effective client satisfaction monitoring and reporting system to evaluate the services provided by the entire Facilities group.
Leads the facilities information and inventory systems function, including university space inventory data, building and infrastructure record drawings, key plans, emergency response plans, and maintenance manuals.
Provides direction and implements change management methodologies to effectively lead and optimize key projects across Facilities.
Mentors and coaches change management in relation to the implementation of business initiatives.
Liaises with academic, administrative and ancillary customers, engineers, architects and external clients to ensure that the facilities needs of the university are being met.
Supports and provides direction to the Senior Facilities Manager in providing strategic leadership to the Facilities Managers working in the geographic zone model. Through the Senior Facilities Manager, oversees the delivery of equal, consistent and effectively prioritized service delivery within the campus zones.
Provides strategic leadership on sustainment of Facilities and University information systems in support of enterprise maintenance management, asset management, stores inventory, space inventory, records drawings, records management, and project management.
Provides strategic leadership and/or oversees development of innovative business solutions and services that integrate data and reporting capabilities to augment decision-making.
Oversees work of various teams performing quality testing of data and information and reconciling across sources, presenting facts and evidence in dashboards to assist in effective evidence-based decision making.
Provides strategic leadership to the Facilities Service Centre who are responsible for handling inbound and outbound calls regarding buildings and grounds.
Responsible for administrative/clerical support services for the Facilities group.
Provides direction in the completion of regulatory and skills development training for all staff within Facilities which includes developing plans, implementing and evaluating, department-wide strategies.
Leads and directs the development of the Facilities Emergency Management Plan, including emergency preparedness exercises for the department in collaboration with SRS, Emergency Management.
Works with SRS and implements consistent health, safety and environmental initiatives, which, includes safety committee, accident investigations, safety training and safety recommendations within the Customer Services and Informatics division.
Responsible for human resource practices including recruitment, orientation, training, performance evaluation, discipline, labor relations and dismissal within the Customer Services and Informatics division in collaboration with Human Resources.
Performs other related duties, including but not limited to:
Representing Facilities on various university committees. Develops working relationships and partnerships with key stakeholders across UBC.
Acting on behalf of the Associate Vice-President, Facilities.

Consequence of Error/Judgement

Facilities plays a key role in enabling the University to achieve its goal of becoming one of the world‘s leading universities. The Director Customer Services and Informatics position is critical to the success of Facilities and the complex services that it provides. The Director must apply judgment, tact and discretion due to the broad and extensive implications for success in the areas of facilities management, project management, business analysis, informatics, information system management, change management, call centre management and clerical support services. The Director plays an important part in the formulation, alignment and implementation of the strategic initiatives and managing the outcomes and impacts on operations and the services they provide.

Failure to ensure alignment and direction for Facilities in this role will negatively impact on the reputation of the University. The consequence of poor decisions have human resources, legal and representational consequences and in addition to costs. Failure to effectively direct major projects that transform business operations through change or to ensure accurate asset information for facilities planning, major capital decisions, or maintenance, construction and renovation activities will lead to the loss of millions of dollars in investment, inefficiencies or unrealized efficiency benefits, and potential safety issues.

A career as Senior Director, Sustainability Disclosure within the Corporate Sustainability team at National Bank means acting as a subject-matter expert and leader in sustainability disclosure and reporting. This role gives you the opportunity to make a positive impact on our organization by leveraging your expertise in sustainability disclosure, governance, risk management, controls and regulatory requirements.

Your role

Lead the sustainability disclosure and reporting program, including its strategy and timelines, as well as the drafting, review and approval processes.

Lead the Bank’s preparation for and response to sustainability-related regulatory requirements and disclosure frameworks to ensure compliant disclosures, advise senior management on key strategic decisions, and oversee the required action plans.

Develop governance, escalation and approval mechanisms, as well as the control framework applicable to sustainability disclosures, to support data quality, traceability, auditability and readiness for external assurance.

Engage teams across Finance, Risk, Legal, Compliance and Internal Audit, as well as data owners, to ensure disclosures are consistent, credible and well supported.

Lead and develop the advisors reporting to you by setting priorities, delivery expectations and quality standards, while supporting their professional development.

Drive collaboration with stakeholders and internal subject-matter experts to support the Bank’s readiness for applicable requirements, including those related to the CSRD, and continuously advance our disclosure practices.
